Cache.//Provider: Redis, or InMemory for a bench with no Redis on it. InMemory holds cart state, tag claims and hub tickets in this process only — cross-till tag arbitration is off, so two tills could sell the same tagged item. Refused outright in Production.

Backup.//Directory: Where BACKUP DATABASE writes and RESTORE reads. The SQL Server service account must be able to write here — a path inside a user profile works for LocalDB only.

OpenIddict.//AllowInsecureHttp: Development only. Production must be HTTPS — an authorization code crossing a shop network in the clear is the whole attack.

Trolleys.//MinStationCode: Which counter codes a shopper may connect to from the phone. This store's shopper counters are 301-320, so the 300 block is reserved for them; everything outside it (the front counter on 001) is refused.
Trolleys.//AutoRegister: Bring an existing counter into app service the first time somebody connects to it.
Trolleys.//AutoCreateStation: Create the counter itself when a code inside the range names one that does not exist. This is what makes the numbering grow on its own once 301-320 are all in use.

Shoppers.//SigningKey: Signs the phone app's access tokens. Development value only, and it is here rather than in user secrets purely so a fresh clone can run the app without setup. Anyone holding this key can mint a token for any shopper, so every other environment MUST set its own — 32 bytes minimum, or the shopper API refuses to issue anything.

Auth.//AdminPassword: Set these to create the first administrator. There is no default: a seeded credential is a published credential. Put the password in user secrets, not here — `dotnet user-secrets set Auth:AdminPassword "<value>"` from src/Retail25.Api. It must be 8+ characters with a digit, or the seeder logs a failure and creates nobody.
Auth.//CashierPassword: Same rule as the administrator: no default, so an unconfigured deployment gets no cashier.
Auth.//AgentClientSecret: Development only. Lets the terminal agent (and the RFID simulator) obtain a token by client_credentials, which is what makes tag reads testable without a reader on the desk. Every other environment must set its own — a shared secret is a published credential.

SelfRegistration.//Enabled: Off by default. New accounts land on Role, whose sales commit nothing at all.

Demo.//SeedCatalogue: Writes ~136 invented products and their RFID tags. Never enable against a real shop's inventory.

Mail.//WriteToLog: Development only. With no relay configured, password-reset links are written to the log — which is a credential in a log, hence the explicit opt-in.

ServerReaders.//Enabled: This process opens the reader connections itself, so a till needs no agent installed. Only works where the server can route to the reader — an API on the shop's own network. Hosted elsewhere, every reader is behind the shop's NAT and this is a slow failure repeated forever; run the terminal agent on the till instead.
ServerReaders.//RefreshSeconds: How often the reader profile table is re-read, so a reader added or disabled in the settings screen is picked up without restarting the API.
